newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi says U.S. envoy confirmation "a great step".
newsitem.headline: Hanoi says U.S. envoy confirmation "a great step".

text.p: Vietnam on Friday hailed the confirmation of a former prisoner of war as the first U.S. ambassador to Hanoi, describing it as "a great step" in relations with its former foe.
The long-delayed nomination of Douglas "Pete" Peterson was confirmed by the Senate in Washington on Thursday after a brief debate and without a recorded vote.
Vietnamese officials welcomed the decision, saying it demonstrated that the majority of Americans supported a desire for a new relationship between the two countries.

"Through this event we can confirm that now the majority of American people and (the) government in general agree to build up a new kind of relationship with Vietnam." said Nguyen Xuan Phong, director of the Americas department at the foreign affairs ministry. "Of course we are pleased."
Peterson's Vietnamese counterpart, envoy-designate Le Van Bang, 50, was equally enthusiastic.

"I think this is a great step, another big step in the process of normalisation of relations between our two countries," he said. "It should be considered as an impetus for better relations in many other fields."

Peterson's appointment, nearly 22 years after the Vietnam war ended, had been held up first by a legal technicality and then by charges that Hanoi's efforts to account for Americans missing in action in Vietnam were inadequate.

Phong dismissed the delays in the process and said Hanoi understood the domestic political environment in Washington which had caused it. "Because of the delay the achievement is more significant," he said.
